candidate.title: Fake "Call Transfer" to Social Security/OIG Scam
candidate.summary: Scammers posing as a retailer, bank, or other agency claim to "transfer" your call directly to the Social Security Administration or its Office of Inspector General, where a second fake agent says your identity has been stolen and pressures you to sign documents or hand over money.
relatedScams: Financial Institution Support Impersonation Account Takeover Scam
safetyTips: Know that legitimate companies and government agencies cannot transfer your phone call directly to SSA or OIG " if they claim they can, it's a scam every time
Hang up and call SSA or the agency directly using a verified number instead of staying on a transferred call
Never sign documents or share personal/financial information based on pressure from an unsolicited or transferred call
Don't trust caller ID alone, since scammers can fake legitimate phone numbers
candidate.howItWorks: The scam begins with a call from someone claiming to represent a retailer, bank, or another agency, often asking about a suspicious purchase or fraudulent activity the consumer didn't make. When the consumer denies making the purchase, the caller "transfers" them to a second scammer posing as an SSA or OIG representative, who claims the consumer's Social Security number has been compromised, linked to identity theft, or used in criminal activity. In one reported case, the fake representative sent a lengthy document to sign, instructed the consumer not to discuss it with anyone, and promised a new Social Security number, all designed to pressure the victim before they had time to verify the story independently.
redFlags: Calls transferred from any company or agency directly to SSA or OIG
Claims that your Social Security number is suspended, compromised, or being reissued
Being told not to discuss the call with anyone else
Pressure to sign a document quickly or share personal information during the same call
Reliance on caller ID, which scammers can spoof to look legitimate
realExamples: A reported call began with someone claiming to be from a major retailer asking about a purchase the consumer didn't make, then transferred the consumer to a person claiming to represent Social Security who said the consumer's identity had been stolen and used to open bank accounts; the caller sent a lengthy document to sign and promised a new Social Security number before the consumer recognized the warning signs and contacted SSA directly.
candidate.source: SSA Office of the Inspector General, https://oig.ssa.gov/scam-alerts/2026-07-29-beware-of-fake-call-transfers-to-social-security-or-oig/

triage.reasoning: This is the same core SSA/OIG "your Social Security number is compromised/suspended" impersonation scam already covered by "Social Security Number Suspended Scam," with the added twist of a fake call transfer from a retailer/bank as the entry vector — a procedural variant rather than a fundamentally new scam pattern. The source states no financial loss occurred in the reported case, supporting a low severity rating.
